ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Julius Caesar

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Adult preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Julius Caesar returns for his adult preventive visit three weeks after his four-week review. The cold has gone. He has had no seizure or spell since starting levetiracetam seven weeks ago and has missed no doses. He takes lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg (added three weeks ago), atorvastatin 80 mg, and aspirin 81 mg without side effects; his home blood pressure readings have been 122 to 132 over 76 to 82. He is sleeping about seven hours a night, has a driver for all journeys, and rides only with a companion. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-06; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Pupils equal and reactive; fundi show mild arteriolar narrowing
No bruit; no thyroid enlargement or nodes
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema
Soft, non-tender; no aortic pulsation felt

Recurrent transient episodes of collapse: six days ago a witnessed collapse with stiffening and jerking of both arms for about a minute, a bitten tongue, and about twenty minutes of confusion, after a rising strange feeling and dizziness; two briefer spells of staring and unresponsiveness in the past eighteen months; cause not yet known (seizure, convulsive syncope, or transient ischemic attack)
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented accounts of falling attacks and fainting fits; it resolves when the cause is found.
Hypertension, stage 2: 152/94 and 148/92 mmHg today; told of high blood pressure about three years ago and never treated
S — Synthetic vascular risk factor; no blood pressure from his lifetime is known.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 158 mg/dL, triglycerides 170 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL
S — Synthetic vascular risk factor; no lipid value from his lifetime is known.

Focal epilepsy with a structural vascular cause: focal impaired-awareness seizures with automatisms, one evolving to a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure, arising from a chronic left temporal cortical infarct, with left temporal sharp waves on EEG
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to the documented falling attacks; the ILAE 2017 seizure types and a structural cause are chosen for teaching and make no claim about what he had.
Chronic left posterior temporal cortical infarct, not recognized before the seizures, with moderate small-vessel white matter disease and a non-stenotic left carotid plaque; no residual deficit
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to the retrospective cerebrovascular hypothesis; it makes no claim about his real brain.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection with low-grade fever and poor sleep, three weeks after starting levetiracetam; rapid COVID-19 and influenza tests negative; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness, chosen to teach cold-remedy choices with hypertension, aspirin, and an antiseizure medicine, and sleep loss as a seizure trigger; it echoes no documented illness.

Follow-up: Hepatitis C, hepatitis B, and HIV results by message. Colonoscopy as booked. Second zoster dose in two to six months. Ten-week chronic-care review in three weeks. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-27: ten-week review: seizure control, lipids on atorvastatin, blood pressure, and driving and safety. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent, prompted by the finding of an old infarct on his scan. He named a health care agent and completed a health care power of attorney form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said he would want full treatment for any new stroke or prolonged seizure, including thrombolysis or thrombectomy if offered, and wants his agent and his neurologist told at once if he is admitted. He chose not to record other treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
